title: KOSPI/KOSDAQ Market Close, Sep 29, 2026: KOSPI Edges Down to 6,870, Samsung Electro-Mechanics and Glass Substrate Names Lead
content:
\n\n

Korea Supply Chain Brief · Market Close, September 29, 2026

KOSPI closed at 6,870.81, down 0.27%, while KOSDAQ closed at 849.80, up 0.38%, as early weakness from U.S. long-term yields and oil prices gave way to bargain-hunting in semiconductor and electronics-component names. Here is what moved the market today.

What moved today

Samsung Electro-Mechanics: $4.9B FC-BGA capex plus $210M MLCC deal

Samsung Electro-Mechanics (KRX: 009150) disclosed a KRW 4.27 trillion investment in FC-BGA production capacity at its Sejong plant for AI servers, its largest-ever single-product investment, with the new line targeting mass production in 2028. The same week, it signed a separate KRW 285 billion (about $210 million) long-term supply agreement for AI server MLCCs and inductors with an unnamed global big-tech customer, bringing its disclosed long-term supply agreements this year to roughly KRW 3.6 trillion combined. (Filing) Electronic-component names including Samsung Electro-Mechanics, Samwha Capacitor, Hanchem, Kocheap and Avatec, and PCB/substrate names including Isu Petasys, TLB, Taesung, Simmtech, Daeduck Electronics and Korea Circuit, moved on the news.

Philoptics: new global order for 2.0mm glass substrate TGV equipment

Philoptics (KOSDAQ: 161580) won an order for next-generation TGV (through-glass via) equipment from a new, unnamed global customer, after its machine hit a 0 ppm defect rate processing thicker 2.0mm glass substrate panels in customer testing. (Announced) Glass-substrate processing and equipment names Philoptics, HB Technology, and Hanbit Laser advanced on the news.

Terabyte: $1M inspection equipment order from Covalent Metrology

Terabyte signed a roughly KRW 1.4 billion (about $1 million) supply agreement with U.S. inspection and metrology firm Covalent Metrology for its EOTPR semiconductor inspection equipment, equal to about 17% of last year's revenue. EOTPR uses terahertz waves to inspect internal connection defects in semiconductor packages without destroying them, covering GPUs, HBM, and advanced packaging structures. (Filing)

SemiFive: $53M AI ASIC development deal with a U.S. fabless customer

SemiFive signed a roughly KRW 70.3 billion (about $53 million) contract with a U.S. AI fabless company to develop a next-generation AI inference accelerator, the company's largest single contract on record and equal to about 58% of last year's revenue. The deal follows a "spec hand-off" model in which SemiFive handles design, packaging, testing, mass production and software once the customer specifies core requirements, targeting tapeout in 2027 and mass production in 2028. (Filing)

Broader semiconductor equipment and materials names advanced

With Samsung Electro-Mechanics' large AI substrate investment and individual orders at SemiFive and Terabyte layered on intraday rebounds in Samsung Electronics and SK hynix, buying spread broadly across semiconductor equipment, materials, and back-end names — Nepes Ark, Wonik IPS, Tes, Jusung Engineering, PSK, Doosan Tesna, DB HiTek, Duksan Hi-Metal, HPSP, Eugene Technology, Hanmi Semiconductor, and Eo Technics among them. (Market move, sentiment-driven)

Quick FAQ

Why did KOSPI open weak today?
Rising U.S. long-term Treasury yields, firmer oil prices, and overnight U.S. tech-stock weakness pressured the open; foreign selling weighed on the index through the session, though semiconductor bargain-hunting narrowed the loss.

What was the single biggest mover today?
Samsung Electro-Mechanics, after disclosing both a KRW 4.27 trillion FC-BGA capex plan and a separate KRW 285 billion MLCC/inductor supply agreement, lifting electronic-component and substrate names broadly.

Which stocks moved on the glass substrate news?
Philoptics, HB Technology, and Hanbit Laser, after Philoptics disclosed a new global order for 2.0mm glass substrate TGV equipment.
